newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Support for Argentina's Menem falls to low - poll.
newsitem.headline: Support for Argentina's Menem falls to low - poll.

text.p: The popularity of Argentine President Carlos Menem has fallen to its lowest level, with only 15 percent backing, according to an opinion poll published Sunday.

The survey by Ricardo Rouvier y Asociados, published in La Nacion newspaper, indicates that the president's support has dropped gradually from a level of 37 percent registered by the polling firm in May 1995. In that month, Menem was reelected with 50 percent of the ballots cast.

The poll comes after the announcement of a series of measures that would increase taxes and reduce worker benefits in an effort to close a widening budget deficit. The measures are expected to be approved by Congress later this month.
Labor unions, who staged a successful 24-hour walkout in protest of the measures last month, plan a 36-hour general strike Sept 26 and 27.

The poll, conducted early this month among 600 respondents, showed Menem's image is worse among the middle class, which would be most hit by the measures. Only 10 percent of the respondents from the middle class were favorable.
The margin of error in the poll was unavailable.
